llm.summary: The skill is mostly a disclosed Apple jobs lookup integration, but its bundled helper can call unrelated Crawlora endpoints with arbitrary methods, which is broader than the stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: Use of CRAWLORA_API_KEY and outbound requests to https://api.crawlora.net/api/v1 is disclosed and coherent for the Apple jobs API, but the generic helper can transmit non-Apple parameters or bodies to Crawlora if misused.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, package manager step, persistence setup, or automatic execution mechanism is present in the inspected artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and reference/endpoints.md describe only GET /apple-jobs/search and GET /apple-jobs/job, while the helper accepts any path, arbitrary -X methods, JSON bodies, and an overrideable API base.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not request elevated privileges, background execution, credential store access, local indexing, or persistent modification of the user environment beyond asking the user to set an API key environment variable.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is read-only Apple careers research, but artifact/scripts/crawlora.sh is a generic Crawlora REST client with examples for Amazon, YouTube, and Google endpoints and no Apple-only allowlist.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. It is reasonable for this skill to send Apple job search terms and job IDs to Crawlora using your CRAWLORA_API_KEY, but the bundled script is more powerful than the Apple jobs workflow and can call other Crawlora routes. Use it only for the documented Apple jobs endpoints unless you intentionally want a generic Crawlora client.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: the helper documentation includes unrelated Crawlora services, which is not needed for an Apple-jobs-only skill.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part: the script concatenates a supplied path onto the API base without validating that it is one of the two documented Apple jobs endpoints.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: arbitrary HTTP methods and JSON bodies are broader than the documented read-only Apple jobs search and detail operations.
[SQP-2] expected: Downgraded: third-party transmission is disclosed in SKILL.md, but the disclosure fits Apple job queries better than the helper's broader generic request capability.
[E1] expected: Expected for purpose: the skill clearly uses Crawlora with an API key to retrieve public Apple job data, so this is a data-boundary consideration rather than malicious behavior.
